content.value_statement: Agent frameworks often hide how tools are registered, validated, and retried. This skill guides a structured review of tool abstractions, schemas, built-in tools, and error feedback.
actual_capabilities: Maps how a framework represents tools through classes, protocols, functions, or Pydantic models.
Compares schema generation methods such as introspection, Pydantic models, decorators, and manual definitions.
Documents registration and discovery patterns, including declarative lists, registries, factories, and toolkits.
Reviews tool execution, validation, error formatting, retry behavior, and LLM self-correction loops.
Produces a structured Markdown analysis with code references and implementation tradeoffs.
limitations: Requires access to the target framework source code for useful results.
Does not execute or test the target framework by itself.
May need manual judgment when frameworks mix several tool patterns.
Focuses on tool interfaces, not provider wire formats or streaming protocols.

use_cases.title: Review a new agent framework
use_cases.description: Identify how the framework defines tools, validates arguments, and exposes tools to the model.

use_cases.title: Compare tool-calling designs
use_cases.description: Build consistent notes across frameworks before selecting patterns for a new implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve retry and error feedback
use_cases.description: Trace how failures are returned to the model and where self-correction can be strengthened.

prompt_templates.title: Map tool basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this framework with tool-interface-analysis. Start with tool modeling, schema generation, registration, execution, and error feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Compare schema methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-interface-analysis to compare how this framework generates tool schemas. Note introspection, Pydantic, decorator, and manual patterns with file references.

prompt_templates.title: Audit retry behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-interface-analysis to trace validation failures, execution errors, retry rules, and LLM self-correction feedback in this codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Create architecture recommendations
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these frameworks with tool-interface-analysis and produce recommendations for a new agent tool layer, including tradeoffs and anti-patterns.

output_examples.input: Analyze a framework that uses Pydantic models for tool arguments and a central registry.
output_examples.output: A Markdown report describing the core tool abstraction, schema generation path, registry flow, validation behavior, and implications for new designs.

output_examples.input: Compare two frameworks with different error feedback mechanisms.
output: A side-by-side summary of feedback quality and retry support.
Concrete notes on where validation errors reach the model.
Recommendations for clearer correction prompts and structured error objects.

output_examples.input: Review built-in tools in an agent framework repository.
output_examples.output: An inventory of tool categories, tool locations, schema methods, sandbox notes, and notable implementation tradeoffs.

best_practices: Start with the framework files that define base tools, schemas, registries, executors, and validation.
Record file and line references for each claim in the output document.
Separate interface design findings from provider protocol findings.
anti_patterns: Do not infer schema behavior from examples without checking implementation code.
Do not mix tool interface analysis with unrelated provider message-format analysis.
Do not treat missing retry behavior as confirmed until execution paths are traced.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes tool modeling, schema generation, registration, execution, validation, error feedback, and retry patterns in agent frameworks.

faq.question: Does it run tools or modify the target framework?
faq.answer: No. It guides code review and documentation. It does not execute framework tools by itself.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a structured Markdown document with sections for modeling, schemas, inventory, registration, execution, and recommendations.

faq.question: Is it useful for comparing frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines consistent categories that make framework comparisons easier and more repeatable.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It can surface sandbox and validation notes, but it is not a full security audit.
